text.p: Brokerage firm Wilson HTM Ltd said it was recommending Macraes Mining Ltd as a buy, reflecting the group's recent expansion of its ore reserves position.

"Buy Macraes. New reserve figures means that Macraes now has the seventh largest ore reserve position of any Australian-Papua New Guinean company," Wilson resources research director, Phil Hutchings said in a report.

Hutchings said Macraes had lifted its ore reserves for its Macraes gold mine in New Zealand to 59.5 million tonnes at 1.58 grams per tonne containing 3.02 million ounces at a 0.7 grams per tonne cut-off grade.
"To put this into perspective, the last published reserve for the Macraes mine was 1.8 million ounces, as at June 1995," Hutchings said.
He said the grade of the reserves was relatively low and the ore had a relatively low metallurgical recovery of only 70 percent to 74 percent.
"For this reason a large-scale mining operation is required to deliver full economies of scale," Hutchings said.
"This is why Macraes has elected to expand the mine to nine milion tonnes a year which will give low mining and milling costs," he said.
Cash costs were expected to be about A$370 an ounce once the expansion was complete, Hutchings said.
He said the expansion would cost NZ$120 million and would lift Macraes' production to about 325,000 ounces a year.
Commissioning of the expansion was targeted for July, 1998.
"The current operations at the Macraes mine are going well with 30,800 ounces produced during the September quarter and on track to produce 130,000 ounces in calendar 1996."
Gold mineralisation at Macraes lay within a shallow dipping shear zone with a 40 kilometre known strike length, he said.
Of this 25 km lay within Macraes Mining tenements and only six km had been thoroughly drilled so far.
Hutchings said the new reserve position for Macraes folowed an intensive drilling programme over the last year.

"Given the company's massive seven-rig exploration programme and the known extent of gold mineralisation on the Macraes tenements, we expect that this figure will be substantially increased over forthcoming years."
